rulings.evidence: Florets are a knife cut of the same whole head, not a form flip to a bagged or frozen product, so the live cauliflower id (5 of 7) is a reuse. Same precedent as shredded carrot to carrots.
butternut-squash is a live board id at 5 of 7, so a reuse and not a proposal; only a vocabulary name row is missing, exactly like the spaghetti-squash ruling on the shelf. Cubed is a cut, not a form.

Second cumin line, in the meatball mix, same rename and same 2.1 g per teaspoon.

eggs is a live board id at 7 of 7, so a reuse; the vocabulary lookup missed only on the singular/qualifier wording. Whole egg out of shell = 50 g, not the 148 g/100 g figure applied to a shell weight.

rulings.raw: 4 tablespoons chopped dill (plus more for garnish)
rulings.evidence: Fresh, not the dried-dill vocabulary row: 4 tbsp chopped into a meatball mix is the fresh herb, and dried is a different price class and roughly a tenfold gram difference per tablespoon, so no alias. New id proposed; board found no commodity but today's captures carry matching products.
Chopped, 4 tbsp, into a raw mix is the fresh herb, so the Fresh Parsley [fresh-parsley] vocabulary row is the same form and an existing id, a reuse. Dried parsley is refused as a form flip.
Zest is the peel of the fruit you buy, so the live lemons id (5 of 7) prices it; the shelf's Orange Zest to orange-juice row is the wrong precedent, juice is not peel. 1 tsp zest = 2 g.

bread-crumbs is a live generic id at 7 of 7 and the same product concept and price class; the vocabulary just names it Panko Breadcrumbs, so a plain-form name row is wanted. Grams supplied for plain crumbs (1 cup = 108 g), not panko, so no weight is inherited.

rulings.raw: 1 pound lean ground bison (beef or lamb)
rulings.evidence: Board reports ABSENT (no commodity, no capture) and no vocabulary row shares a core word, so a new id goes to the registrar. Bison is a different species and price class from any beef or lamb id and must not be aliased onto one.
Optional condiment offered at serving with no quantity anywhere in the source, so it cannot be costed or weighed; inventing an amount would move the published macros.
Same as tzatziki: optional at serving with no quantity. harissa-paste (2 of 7) is the correct id the day a version quantifies it, but nothing can be priced against a blank amount.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Board reports ABSENT: no commodity claims it and no capture matches. It is not a spelling variant of anything already priced - bison is a distinct species sold at 2 to 3 times ground beef, so ground-beef-8020, any lean-beef id and any lamb id are all different price classes, not synonyms; the only word overlap ('ground') belongs to the cut, not the meat. If you reject, note the source line itself sanctions 'beef or lamb', so an existing lean ground beef id is the sanctioned human substitution rather than a silent bridge by me.

The vocabulary carries only Dried Dill [dried-dill] and the board found no commodity for dill, though today's captures carry matching products so it is priceable. Fresh herb bunches and dried spice jars are different price classes and differ roughly tenfold in grams per tablespoon, so an alias onto dried-dill would be a form flip. This mirrors the existing fresh-parsley / dried-parsley pair, which is the estate's own precedent for keeping the two separate.
